name: Identity Card Number
issuer: the DNIC (National Direction of Civil Identification)
note: Uruguay's sheet (its government's own sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers'; the OECD's index page sits behind a bot check and wasn't opened, the sheet itself came straight back)), read 2026-10-30: a person without a RUT is identified for tax by the identity card the DNIC issues; its number is 7 digits and a verification digit, written without points or hyphens. The verification rule isn't given, so `check` is left out. Read as given on application for the card (when, to whom and at what age isn't in the sheet; citizens and residents are the game's reading); foreigners without a card get a 9-digit NIE from the tax authority (not modelled). The name and issuer are as the sheet gives them, in English.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Uruguay: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: IDCard: Identity Card for Physical Persons: a Card issued by the National Office ... This number is granted by the DNIC (National Direction of Civil Identification), and is formed by 7 numbers, plus ... a verifying digit. For our RUT records, we register the number without any points or hyphens.
